takeaways: Nvidia is shifting AI infrastructure financing toward institutional capital, effectively securitizing compute as a long-term asset while pressuring hyperscalers to self-fund power generation and hardware development.
China is aggressively stimulating its private sector and refining monetary policy to combat deflationary pressures, even as excess industrial capacity threatens to intensify global trade tensions.

Market sentiment is cooling toward AI-hardware valuations as investors demand sustained profitability, while corporate shifts in bond-buying and restructuring signal a broader pivot toward capital preservation.
day_verdict: Major day — market-moving events; read carefully.

items.title: China's central bank promises policy support, stronger countercyclical adjustments
bullets: The PBOC is shifting its operational target rate from the seven-day repo rate (DR007) to the overnight rate (DR001), with overnight transactions now comprising over 90 percent of money market repo trading.

Despite global tightening trends, the PBOC plans to implement incremental policy measures to maintain ample liquidity and low financing costs, signaling a divergence from the hawkish bias observed in the U.S. Federal Reserve.
items.reason: Significant shift in Chinese monetary policy framework and liquidity management.

items.title: PBOC Warns of Imported Inflation Risks, Sees Overseas Rate Hikes as Potentially Milder Than Past Episodes
bullets: The PBOC identifies a convergence of inflationary pressures driven by Middle East geopolitical conflicts, rising commodity prices, and increased demand for power and semiconductors linked to the AI investment boom.

Chinese authorities assess that current global monetary tightening cycles will likely be milder than historical episodes, suggesting a lower probability of severe shocks to international financial markets.
items.reason: Provides critical insight into China's assessment of global inflation and systemic financial risks.

items.title: Iran to join BRICS development bank soon, central bank governor says
bullets: Iran's impending membership in the New Development Bank (NDB) underscores a strategic push by BRICS nations to establish alternative financial channels that bypass the U.S. dollar-denominated system.

The move highlights a broader trend of emerging economies seeking to conduct trade in national currencies, potentially impacting long-term demand for dollar-based settlement infrastructure in sanctioned regions.
items.reason: Geopolitical shift in financial infrastructure and de-dollarization efforts.

items.title: Cisco's stock drops despite earnings, revenue beat
bullets: Cisco reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $1.22 per share on $17.25 billion in revenue, both exceeding analyst estimates of $1.17 and $16.82 billion respectively.
Despite strong guidance—including a projected revenue increase from hyperscalers to $7.5 billion in fiscal 2027—shares fell as investors reacted to the stock's 60% year-to-date run-up.
items.reason: Major tech bellwether earnings reaction

items.title: Cerebras stock plunges 14% after second earnings report following IPO
bullets: Cerebras missed second-quarter core revenue expectations, reporting $180 million against a $194 million consensus, despite raising its full-year core revenue outlook to $880-$890 million.

The company reported a significant net loss of $450.5 million, largely driven by $386.6 million in stock-compensation costs, even as management emphasized strong demand for its 'fast inference' AI chips.
items.reason: High-growth AI stock volatility

items.title: SK Hynix halts bond buying, shifts cash to bank deposits in blow to S.Korean credit market
bullets: SK Hynix has abruptly ceased its corporate bond-buying activities, opting instead to move significant cash reserves into commercial bank deposits, which creates immediate liquidity concerns for the South Korean short-term credit market.

The strategic shift by the major AI memory chip supplier suggests a pivot toward prioritizing higher shareholder returns, potentially signaling a broader cooling of corporate demand for fixed-income securities in the region.
items.reason: Significant liquidity shift in regional credit markets

items.title: US yield curve twists expose Trump's and Bessent's rate dilemma
bullets: Recent volatility in the US yield curve is complicating the policy outlook for the administration, forcing a delicate balancing act between managing borrowing costs and addressing inflationary pressures.

The current market environment highlights a structural dilemma for policymakers, as shifting yield expectations threaten to constrain fiscal flexibility and impact broader economic growth projections.
items.reason: Direct impact on US fiscal policy and interest rate outlook

items.title: PBOC Q2 Monetary Policy Report: H1 GDP Grows 4.7%, Yuan Strengthens 3% vs Dollar, Creates 1 Trillion Yuan Private Enterprise Relending Facility
bullets: The PBOC has launched a 1 trillion yuan relending facility specifically for private enterprises, signaling a targeted effort to bolster the private sector amid ongoing economic structural adjustments.

Monetary authorities have refined interest rate control by narrowing the repo corridor to 50 basis points and lowering structural tool rates by 0.25 percentage points to reduce corporate financing costs.
items.reason: Significant shift in monetary policy and liquidity support.

items.title: Excess savings are driving the new ‘China shock’
bullets: Unlike the original China shock driven by low-cost labor, this new iteration is fueled by domestic technological upgrading and a persistent lack of internal consumer demand.

Investors should note that excess domestic savings are forcing manufacturers to export surplus capacity, potentially intensifying global trade tensions and impacting international manufacturing margins.
items.reason: Structural shift in China's export dynamics impacting global trade.

items.title: Oracle plans more layoffs weeks after spending most of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget
bullets: Oracle is initiating a new round of layoffs to reduce payroll before the second fiscal quarter, following a year where it already eliminated 21,000 positions, representing 13% of its total workforce.

With $1.8 billion of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget already exhausted, the company faces a potential financial squeeze that may necessitate a second major restructuring plan within three years to cover ongoing severance costs.
items.reason: Signals potential margin pressure and operational instability despite massive AI-driven capital expenditure.

items.title: Trump Says He Has Told Big Tech Companies to Build Their Own Power Plants
bullets: The administration is pressuring major technology firms to self-fund power generation for data centers, citing the inability of the aging national grid to handle the massive electricity demands of AI infrastructure.

This policy shift, intended to shield consumers from rising utility costs, could significantly alter the capital expenditure profiles and long-term operational strategies for hyperscalers like Microsoft and Google.
items.reason: Direct regulatory intervention threatens the scalability and cost structure of the AI data center boom.

items.title: Cerebras shares plummet 16% after results fail to impress investors
bullets: Cerebras Systems experienced a significant 16% decline in share price following an earnings report that failed to meet heightened investor expectations for the AI hardware challenger.

The market reaction underscores growing investor sensitivity to valuation premiums for AI-focused hardware firms, as participants demand clear evidence of sustained revenue growth and competitive differentiation against established incumbents.
items.reason: Market sentiment shift for AI hardware

items.title: How much time does AI save at work? New Census Bureau data breaks it down.
bullets: New U.S. Census Bureau data indicates that 55% of workers currently utilize AI, with one-third of these users reporting time savings of one to two hours per assignment.

While productivity gains are emerging, the data highlights a 'J-curve' adoption effect where initial learning requirements can temporarily decrease efficiency before long-term output gains are realized by firms.
items.reason: Empirical evidence of AI productivity impact

items.title: Alphabet’s stock slips as Nvidia’s $500 billion financing deal threatens custom chips
bullets: Nvidia is reportedly orchestrating a massive $500 billion financing initiative involving firms like Apollo Global and Blackstone to subsidize data center infrastructure and power generation for its customers.

This strategy creates a competitive headwind for hyperscalers like Alphabet and Microsoft, as it potentially lowers the barrier to entry for smaller AI cloud providers while incentivizing continued reliance on Nvidia hardware over proprietary custom silicon.
items.reason: Significant shift in business model impacting competitive landscape and capital allocation.

items.title: Meta and Nvidia plant 'very firm flag' in open-weight AI race led by Chinese Labs
bullets: Nvidia has launched its Nemotron 3.5 Lightning model, positioning it as a 'truly open source' offering by providing full access to training datasets, techniques, and model weights to developers.

This move represents a strategic pivot to counter the influence of Chinese AI labs and proprietary models from OpenAI, aiming to solidify Nvidia's ecosystem dominance by fostering widespread adoption of its open-weight architecture.
items.reason: Strategic shift in AI software strategy to maintain market leadership against open-source competition.

items.title: EVs dominate China’s car market: 5 takeaways from the country's latest auto sales data
bullets: New energy vehicles reached a 65.1% market share in China during July, yet total passenger car sales plummeted 20.3% year-over-year, signaling a severe contraction in the broader automotive sector.

Geely has successfully challenged BYD for market leadership, with its Xingyuan electric hatchback becoming the top-selling model, while BYD's overall passenger car sales declined by more than 10% in the first half of 2025.
items.reason: Significant market share shift and volume contraction in the world's largest EV market.

items.title: EVs Excluded From South Korea's Version of IRA, Raising Concerns Across Battery Industry
bullets: The South Korean government's exclusion of electric vehicles from its new Domestic Production Tax Credit program threatens the competitiveness of domestic automakers like Hyundai and Kia against rising Chinese imports.

Industry analysts warn of a potential cascading negative impact on the domestic battery supply chain, as lower EV sales volumes for local manufacturers could reduce demand for locally produced battery components.
items.reason: Policy shift impacting competitive landscape for major automakers and battery suppliers.

items.title: Nvidia found a new way to keep the AI boom funded: your retirement money
bullets: Nvidia is partnering with major asset managers like BlackRock, Apollo, and KKR to mobilize over $500 billion in private capital, effectively shifting AI infrastructure financing from corporate balance sheets to institutional retirement funds.

This model treats AI compute as a long-term productive asset—similar to a toll road or power plant—allowing for debt securitization based on future cash flows from compute leasing, rather than relying on rapidly depreciating hardware.
items.reason: Significant structural shift in how AI infrastructure is financed at scale.

items.title: AI Infrastructure Boom Drives Industrial Leasing Demand Beyond Data Centers, Cushman & Wakefield Finds
bullets: Data center-related industrial leasing reached 13.5 million square feet in 2025, a 44% increase from 2024, as the AI ecosystem creates massive secondary demand for manufacturers of electrical, cooling, and power infrastructure.

The broader economic impact is substantial, with the data center supply chain supporting an estimated 81,000 to 124,000 jobs and generating $11.6 billion in annual gross economic output across major U.S. markets.
items.reason: Highlights the broader industrial real estate investment implications of the AI boom.

items.title: SpaceX could make $500 billion in 2028, Elon Musk says
bullets: CEO Elon Musk projects that SpaceX's AI-related revenue will surpass all other business segments by Q4 2026, with the company aiming to scale AI compute capacity to 10 gigawatts by the end of next year.

The company is pivoting toward a massive AI-centric infrastructure strategy, including the 'Terafab' semiconductor manufacturing complex and plans to deploy one million 'Starmind' AI satellites to support orbital data centers.
items.reason: Major strategic pivot to AI with significant revenue implications.

items.title: VinSpace Announces Launch Contract with SpaceX, Marking a New Milestone for Vietnam's Space Industry
bullets: Vietnam-based VinSpace has secured a launch contract with SpaceX for a 2027 Transporter rideshare mission, signaling the company's intent to develop full-stack aerospace capabilities including satellite design and manufacturing.

The partnership serves as a critical step for VinSpace to validate in-house developed technologies and expand its satellite engineering footprint, marking a notable entry for Vietnam into the commercial space value chain.
items.reason: Expansion of commercial space access for emerging market players.
